as_told.title: Neil deGrasse Tyson debunk of Apollo 17 sightings

plain: The claim is that small blue lights seen in photos from the Moon missions, and the flashes of light the astronaut Buzz Aldrin said he saw inside his cabin, were caused by cosmic rays, fast particles from space hitting cameras and eyes. Michael Shermer, a well-known skeptic, says the Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb thinks so and that Loeb is "probably right". The physicist Maaneli Derakhshani also credits Loeb, tying it to a trio of blue lights from the Apollo 17 mission. Michels, on the same episode, credits instead the astrophysicist Neil deGrasse Tyson, who he says treated the Apollo 17 sightings as "case closed, cosmic rays". If the explanation holds, these lights would be ordinary physics rather than anything flying near the Moon.
